speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether there has been an increase in the number of artificial intelligence voice cloning scams in Singapore; (b) how many of such scams have occurred this year to date; and (c) how is the Government dealing with these types of scams, including in the areas of enforcement, public education and implementation of technological solutions to prevent their occurrence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Regardless of scam typology, the SPF works closely with stakeholders, such as local telecommunication companies and messaging application companies, to prevent criminals from using our communication channels as conduits for scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: As we have mentioned several times in the House, the fight against scams requires a whole-of-society effort.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For example, social media platforms and messaging apps should introduce enhanced user verification measures to weed out inauthentic accounts and prevent scammers from abusing them to perpetrate scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: On its part, the public has to remain vigilant and take the necessary steps to Add, Check, Tell (ACT) against scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Everyone should make a proactive effort to add security features to their devices to protect themselves against scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For example, add anti-virus software and update our mobile devices with the latest security patches.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: If you suspect that you have fallen prey to a scam, call and tell your bank immediately and ask the bank to activate the "kill-switch" to protect your banking account.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: If each of us play our part, we can collectively have a better chance of reducing our losses to scammers.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Can I clarify how many voice-cloning scam reports were actually received by the Police in the past year?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Scammers can use this cloned voice to trick friends and family members of these persons into transferring money to them.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I recently checked the ScamAlert telegram channel and website, but do not see any mention of voice-cloning scams.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Do the National Crime Prevention Council and other agencies plan to educate Singaporeans about this new scam and how to protect themselves?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: For example, not assuming that the familiar voice on the other end of the line is the person they know and by establishing a common passcode among family members.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Lastly, does the Ministry for Home Affairs scan the horizon for new scam technologies and start to take crime prevention measures before the first police reports start coming in?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As I have said, the number is small.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: With regard to the education efforts and scam technologies, yes, we continue to update and also look at how we work with the different stakeholders in the community, including the public.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the same time, we are also developing our capabilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For example, we are developing technical measures in collaboration with the industry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, essentially, we will do our part to enhance our capabilities as the scammers themselves do so.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: However, as I shared have earlier, it is important for us to continue to engage the ground.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I am pleased to share that even at the different Neighbourhood Police Centres, I can see the Police officers engaging the ground – from common layperson to people with knowledge of it – so that the whole society is being protected.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Because I think for the scammers, this is an opportunity for them to commit crimes or to steal money from people.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But on our part, we have to protect our people.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we will continue to work hard to engage the whole society.
